verses.en: Boast not thyself of to morrow; for thou knowest not what a day may bring forth.
verses.pt: Não te glories do dia de amanhã; porque não sabes o que produzirá o dia.
verses.en_web: Don’t boast about tomorrow; for you don’t know what a day may bring.
verses.en_bbe: Do not make a noise about tomorrow, for you are not certain what a day's outcome may be.

verses.en: Let another man praise thee, and not thine own mouth; a stranger, and not thine own lips.
verses.pt: Seja outro o que te louve, e não a tua boca; o estranho, e não os teus lábios.
verses.en_web: Let another man praise you, and not your own mouth; a stranger, and not your own lips.
verses.en_bbe: Let another man give you praise, and not your mouth; one who is strange to you, and not your lips.

verses.en: A stone is heavy, and the sand weighty; but a fool’s wrath is heavier than them both.
verses.pt: Pesada é a pedra, e a areia também; mas a ira do insensato é mais pesada do que elas ambas.
verses.en_web: A stone is heavy, and sand is a burden; but a fool’s provocation is heavier than both.
verses.en_bbe: A stone has great weight, and sand is crushing; but the wrath of the foolish is of greater weight than these.

verses.en: Wrath is cruel, and anger is outrageous; but who is able to stand before envy?
verses.pt: Cruel é o furor, e impetuosa é a ira; mas quem pode resistir à inveja?
verses.en_web: Wrath is cruel, and anger is overwhelming; but who is able to stand before jealousy?
verses.en_bbe: Wrath is cruel, and angry feeling an overflowing stream; but who does not give way before envy?

verses.en: Open rebuke is better than secret love.
verses.pt: Melhor é a repreensão aberta do que o amor encoberto.
verses.en_web: Better is open rebuke than hidden love.
verses.en_bbe: Better is open protest than love kept secret.

verses.en: Faithful are the wounds of a friend; but the kisses of an enemy are deceitful.
verses.pt: Fiéis são as feridas dum amigo; mas os beijos dum inimigo são enganosos.
verses.en_web: Faithful are the wounds of a friend; although the kisses of an enemy are profuse.
verses.en_bbe: The wounds of a friend are given in good faith, but the kisses of a hater are false.

verses.en: The full soul loatheth an honeycomb; but to the hungry soul every bitter thing is sweet.
verses.pt: O que está farto despreza o favo de mel; mas para o faminto todo amargo é doce.
verses.en_web: A full soul loathes a honeycomb; but to a hungry soul, every bitter thing is sweet.
verses.en_bbe: The full man has no use for honey, but to the man in need of food every bitter thing is sweet.

verses.en: As a bird that wandereth from her nest, so is a man that wandereth from his place.
verses.pt: Qual a ave que vagueia longe do seu ninho, tal é o homem que anda vagueando longe do seu lugar.
verses.en_web: As a bird that wanders from her nest, so is a man who wanders from his home.
verses.en_bbe: Like a bird wandering from the place of her eggs is a man wandering from his station.

verses.en: Ointment and perfume rejoice the heart: so doth the sweetness of a man’s friend by hearty counsel.
verses.pt: O óleo e o perfume alegram o coração; assim é o doce conselho do homem para o seu amigo.
verses.en_web: Perfume and incense bring joy to the heart; so does earnest counsel from a man’s friend.
verses.en_bbe: Oil and perfume make glad the heart, and the wise suggestion of a friend is sweet to the soul.

verses.en: Thine own friend, and thy father’s friend, forsake not; neither go into thy brother’s house in the day of thy calamity: for better is a neighbour that is near than a brother far off.
verses.pt: Não abandones o teu amigo, nem o amigo de teu pai; nem entres na casa de teu irmão no dia de tua adversidade. Mais vale um vizinho que está perto do que um irmão que está longe.
verses.en_web: Don’t forsake your friend and your father’s friend. Don’t go to your brother’s house in the day of your disaster: better is a neighbor who is near than a distant brother.
verses.en_bbe: Do not give up your friend and your father's friend; and do not go into your brother's house in the day of your trouble: better is a neighbour who is near than a brother far off.

verses.en: My son, be wise, and make my heart glad, that I may answer him that reproacheth me.
verses.pt: Sê sábio, filho meu, e alegra o meu coração, para que eu tenha o que responder àquele que me vituperar.
verses.en_web: Be wise, my son, and bring joy to my heart, then I can answer my tormentor.
verses.en_bbe: My son, be wise and make my heart glad, so that I may give back an answer to him who puts me to shame.

verses.en: A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself; but the simple pass on, and are punished.
verses.pt: O prudente vê o mal e se esconde; mas os insensatos passam adiante e sofrem a pena.
verses.en_web: A prudent man sees danger and takes refuge; but the simple pass on, and suffer for it.
verses.en_bbe: The sharp man sees the evil and takes cover: the simple go straight on and get into trouble.

verses.en: Take his garment that is surety for a stranger, and take a pledge of him for a strange woman.
verses.pt: Tira a roupa àquele que fica por fiador do estranho, e toma penhor daquele que se obriga por uma estrangeira.
verses.en_web: Take his garment when he puts up collateral for a stranger. Hold it for a wayward woman!
verses.en_bbe: Take a man's clothing if he makes himself responsible for a strange man, and get an undertaking from him who gives his word for strange men.

verses.en: He that blesseth his friend with a loud voice, rising early in the morning, it shall be counted a curse to him.
verses.pt: O que bendiz ao seu amigo em alta voz, levantando-se de madrugada, isso lhe será contado como maldição.
verses.en_web: He who blesses his neighbor with a loud voice early in the morning, it will be taken as a curse by him.
verses.en_bbe: He who gives a blessing to his friend with a loud voice, getting up early in the morning, will have it put to his account as a curse.

verses.en: A continual dropping in a very rainy day and a contentious woman are alike.
verses.pt: A goteira contínua num dia chuvoso e a mulher rixosa são semelhantes;
verses.en_web: A continual dropping on a rainy day and a contentious wife are alike:
verses.en_bbe: Like an unending dropping on a day of rain is a bitter-tongued woman.

verses.en: Whosoever hideth her hideth the wind, and the ointment of his right hand, which bewrayeth itself.
verses.pt: retê-la é reter o vento, ou segurar o óleo com a destra.
verses.en_web: restraining her is like restraining the wind, or like grasping oil in his right hand.
verses.en_bbe: He who keeps secret the secret of his friend, will get himself a name for good faith.

verses.en: Iron sharpeneth iron; so a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend.
verses.pt: Afia-se o ferro com o ferro; assim o homem afia o rosto do seu amigo.
verses.en_web: Iron sharpens iron; so a man sharpens his friend’s countenance.
verses.en_bbe: Iron makes iron sharp; so a man makes sharp his friend.

verses.en: Whoso keepeth the fig tree shall eat the fruit thereof: so he that waiteth on his master shall be honoured.
verses.pt: O que cuida da figueira comerá do fruto dela; e o que vela pelo seu senhor será honrado.
verses.en_web: Whoever tends the fig tree shall eat its fruit. He who looks after his master shall be honored.
verses.en_bbe: Whoever keeps a fig-tree will have its fruit; and the servant waiting on his master will be honoured.

verses.en: As in water face answereth to face, so the heart of man to man.
verses.pt: Como na água o rosto corresponde ao rosto, assim o coração do homem ao homem.
verses.en_web: Like water reflects a face, so a man’s heart reflects the man.
verses.en_bbe: Like face looking at face in water, so are the hearts of men to one another.

verses.en: Hell and destruction are never full; so the eyes of man are never satisfied.
verses.pt: O Seol e o Abadom nunca se fartam, e os olhos do homem nunca se satisfazem.
verses.en_web: Sheol and Abaddon are never satisfied; and a man’s eyes are never satisfied.
verses.en_bbe: The underworld and Abaddon are never full, and the eyes of man have never enough.

verses.en: As the fining pot for silver, and the furnace for gold; so is a man to his praise.
verses.pt: O crisol é para a prata, e o forno para o ouro, e o homem é provado pelos louvores que recebe.
verses.en_web: The crucible is for silver, and the furnace for gold; but man is refined by his praise.
verses.en_bbe: The heating-pot is for silver and the oven-fire for gold, and a man is measured by what he is praised for.

verses.en: Though thou shouldest bray a fool in a mortar among wheat with a pestle, yet will not his foolishness depart from him.
verses.pt: Ainda que pisasses o insensato no gral entre grãos pilados, contudo não se apartaria dele a sua estultícia.
verses.en_web: Though you grind a fool in a mortar with a pestle along with grain, yet his foolishness will not be removed from him.
verses.en_bbe: Even if a foolish man is crushed with a hammer in a vessel among crushed grain, still his foolish ways will not go from him.

verses.en: Be thou diligent to know the state of thy flocks, and look well to thy herds.
verses.pt: Procura conhecer o estado das tuas ovelhas; cuida bem dos teus rebanhos;
verses.en_web: Know well the state of your flocks, and pay attention to your herds:
verses.en_bbe: Take care to have knowledge about the condition of your flocks, looking well after your herds;

verses.en: For riches are not for ever: and doth the crown endure to every generation?
verses.pt: porque as riquezas não duram para sempre; e duraria a coroa de geração em geração?
verses.en_web: for riches are not forever, nor does the crown endure to all generations.
verses.en_bbe: For wealth is not for ever, and money does not go on for all generations.

verses.en: The hay appeareth, and the tender grass sheweth itself, and herbs of the mountains are gathered.
verses.pt: Quando o feno é removido, e aparece a erva verde, e recolhem-se as ervas dos montes,
verses.en_web: The hay is removed, and the new growth appears, the grasses of the hills are gathered in.
verses.en_bbe: The grass comes up and the young grass is seen, and the mountain plants are got in.

verses.en: The lambs are for thy clothing, and the goats are the price of the field.
verses.pt: os cordeiros te proverão de vestes, e os bodes, do preço do campo.
verses.en_web: The lambs are for your clothing, and the goats are the price of a field.
verses.en_bbe: The lambs are for your clothing, and the he-goats make the value of a field:

verses.en: And thou shalt have goats’ milk enough for thy food, for the food of thy household, and for the maintenance for thy maidens.
verses.pt: E haverá bastante leite de cabras para o teu sustento, para o sustento da tua casa e das tuas criadas.
verses.en_web: There will be plenty of goats’ milk for your food, for your family’s food, and for the nourishment of your servant girls.
verses.en_bbe: There will be goats' milk enough for your food, and for the support of your servant-girls.
